requirement_conflicts.description:
AC-05 states count_text("  
 
") == {"char_count": 6, "line_count": 2, "non_empty_line_count": 0, "word_count": 0}. BC-02 mandates the sole normalisation order (strip one leading U+FEFF, replace all CRLF with LF, then all remaining lone CR with LF) and BC-08 defines char_count as len() of the normalised text. The input "  
 
" holds 7 raw code points (space space CR LF space CR LF); after BC-02 it is "  
 
" with 5 code points, so any mapping satisfying both BC-02 and BC-08 yields char_count == 5, never 6. The same AC-05 line_count == 2 and non_empty_line_count == 0 agree with BC-04/BC-05/BC-06. The delivery implements 5 and the run's own coding-report.json requirement_conflicts reports the identical conflict (AC-05 vs BC-02/BC-08); examples/text-stats/README.md line 139 documents the same discrepancy. No set of expectations was silently chosen here; the same-call char_count expectation is mutually exclusive.
